title: Honest Brokers in AI Regulation: How Public Comments Introduce Evidence to Regulators
abstract: arXiv:2611.21948v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The regulation of Artificial Intelligence is susceptible to various forms of capture by industry actors that hold undue influence over the policymaking process, due in part to their information advantage in developing these technologies. In the following paper, we investigate the roles of public commenters in providing evidence to potential regulation in the USA. We build a corpus of 40 potential regulations, and 2,664 public comments submitted by a variety of stakeholders. We computationally process these texts to extract evidence meant to inform regulators, in the form of formal citations and informal references. We find significant differences in the type and amount of evidence supplied: Holding comment length constant, business commenters introduce altogether less evidence, and government, university, and civil society commenters provide significantly more research and legal sources. translated_title: 人工智能监管中的诚实经纪人：公众意见如何向监管者引入证据
translated_abstract: 人工智能的监管容易被行业行为者以各种形式“俘获”，这些行业行为者对政策制定过程拥有不当影响力，部分原因在于他们在开发这些技术方面具有信息优势。在本文中，我们研究了公众意见提交者在美国向潜在监管提供证据方面所扮演的角色。我们构建了一个包含40项潜在监管规则以及各类利益相关者提交的2,664份公众意见的语料库。我们对这些文本进行计算化处理，以正式引用和非正式引用的形式提取旨在为监管者提供参考的证据。我们发现所提供证据的类型和数量存在显著差异：在控制意见长度不变的情况下，企业意见提交者总体上引入的证据较少，而政府、大学和公民社会的意见提交者提供了显著更多的研究类和法律类来源。被引用研究的发表状态几乎……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究通过计算分析美国40项潜在AI监管规则的2,664份公众意见发现，企业提交者引入的证据总体较少，而政府、大学和公民社会提交者提供了显著更多的研究和法律来源，表明非行业利益相关者可作为对抗行业俘获的“诚实经纪人”。
en_tdlr: Analyzing 2,664 public comments on 40 potential U.S. AI regulations, this study finds that business commenters introduce less evidence overall, while government, university, and civil society commenters provide significantly more research and legal sources, positioning non-industry stakeholders as honest brokers against industry capture in AI regulation.
